summary: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error.
takeaways: Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks.
In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error.

Needing neither per-device calibration nor gradients through the hardware, and improving with more capable models, optics as code offers a practical route to large, scalable optical neural networks and a general tool for calibrating and optimizing optical experiments.
